name: ElevenLabs
title: ElevenLabs TTS
description: Speak text aloud in a chosen voice. Outputs base64 MP3.
whenToUse: Read TEXT ALOUD in one voice: a narration, an announcement, a spoken reply. It performs words that are already written, so use it when the words exist and only the voice is needed. For several speakers in one clip use ElevenLabs Dialogue; for the sound of a thing rather than speech use Sound Effects.

voiceId.title: Voice ID
voiceId.description: Any voice id from your ElevenLabs library. Leave blank for a default narrator voice — the same premade voice the code version fell back to, so an unset field keeps working.

modelId.title: Model
modelId.description: Override the TTS model. Leave blank for the package default.

stability.title: Stability
stability.description: 0 is most expressive, 0.5 natural, 1 most consistent. ElevenLabs accepts ONLY these three values on this model, so anything else falls back to 0.5.

outputFormat.title: Output Format
outputFormat.description: Audio encoding, e.g. mp3_44100_128. Leave blank for the account default.

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only a signed-in caller may run this step. Leave off and it runs for whoever the workflow's trigger admitted, which is the usual answer.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller's account must carry, as noun:verb (finance:approve, payments:refund). Leave blank to require only that they are signed in.

package.name: elevenlabs
package.packageFile:
# ELEVENLABS, fully declarative — all five nodes.
#
# ALL FIVE, not four, and that is forced rather than ambitious: they share ONE credential, and
# declaration is all-or-nothing per package (`registerCredentialType` is first-wins and silent, so a
# credentials/*.yaml alongside a live registerCredential() means one of them vanishes at random). So
# SpeechToText could not be left behind — which is why `encoding: multipart` was built first.
#
# FOUR SHAPES, ONE PACKAGE:
#   TTS, Dialogue, Music, SoundEffects   POST JSON, receive raw audio bytes → transport: binary
#   SpeechToText                         POST a FORM carrying the audio file → encoding: multipart
#
# ONE PATH DROPPED, deliberately, and it is worth reading before assuming it was an oversight. The TTS
# node also carried a MULTI-SPEAKER COMPAT path: it sniffed [DETECTIVE]: labels out of the text, mapped
# them to hardcoded voice pools, tried /text-to-dialogue, and on failure fell back to one TTS call per
# segment with the mp3 buffers CONCATENATED. That concatenation is byte work no manifest can describe.
#
# It is gone because its reason is gone. The path existed to preserve the MurderMystery app, which is now
# in _legacy/; `characterId` and `characterGender` appear nowhere in apps/ outside the node's own files;
# and the service's own header already said "for general multi-speaker work prefer the dedicated
# ElevenLabs Dialogue node", which is in this package and takes explicit per-line voices. So the
# capability is not lost, it moved to the node built for it.

name: elevenlabs
displayName: ElevenLabs
description: Speech, dialogue, music and sound effects from ElevenLabs
version: 2.0.0
category: media
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1768540562/gravity/icons/elevanlabs.jpg

features:
  - Text to speech, dialogue, music and sound effects
  - Transcription with word-level timings

allowedHosts:
  - api.elevenlabs.io

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.6.0"
  credential: [apiKeyHeader]
  # `binary` for the four generators, `json` for transcription's reply.
  transport: [binary, json]
  encoding: [multipart]

credentials.elevenlabsCredential.yaml:
# The TYPE NAME is kept exactly as it was when these nodes lived in `ingest`, so credentials already
# stored against it keep resolving. A credential is selected by type name, so renaming it would leave
# every existing workflow authenticating with nothing.
name: elevenlabsCredential
displayName: ElevenLabs
description: ElevenLabs API credentials for text-to-speech, sound effects, and transcription

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your ElevenLabs API key from the dashboard (Profile then API Keys)
    placeholder: Enter your ElevenLabs API key

shared.audio.yaml:
# THE AUDIO OUTPUT, shared by the four generators.
#
# `response` is the BINARY reply handed over as { base64, contentType } — what `transport: binary`
# produces, and the same shape a `multipart` file part consumes, so bytes have ONE representation
# everywhere they travel in this platform.
#
# Shared because four nodes emit the identical object and a fifth will: the day the shape changes, it
# changes once.

out: >-
  return { data: response.base64, mimeType: response.contentType || 'audio/mpeg', fileName: 'audio.mp3' }
shared.credential.yaml:
# ElevenLabs authenticates with `xi-api-key`, on every call in the package.
#
# Shared because repeating it five times is five chances to mistype the header name, and a wrong header
# is a 401 that reads like a bad key rather than a bad manifest.

scheme: apiKeyHeader
header: xi-api-key
value: "{{ credentials.elevenlabsCredential.apiKey }}"

files.api/run.yaml:
# ONE POST, the SINGLE-VOICE path — which is what this node is for. The multi-speaker compat path is
# deliberately not here; package.yaml says why, and ElevenLabs Dialogue supersedes it.
#
# THE VOICE IS IN THE PATH, which is why the url is an expression: an unset voiceId must fall back rather
# than produce `/text-to-speech//` — a URL that 404s about a missing route instead of a missing voice. The
# fallback is the code version's own default narrator (the first premade male voice, Daniel).
#
# STABILITY IS AN ENUM OF THREE on this model, and the service normalised anything else to 0.5 rather than
# letting the vendor reject it. Transcribed, because a rejected request is a failed node.

- name: speak
  method: POST
  url: >-
    return 'https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/text-to-speech/'
      + (config.voiceId || 'onwK4e9ZLuTAKqWW03F9')
  credential: { $ref: credential }

  body:
    text: "{{ config.text }}"
    model_id: "{{ config.modelId }}"
    voice_settings:
      stability: >-
        return [0, 0.5, 1].includes(config.stability) ? config.stability : 0.5

  query:
    output_format: "{{ config.outputFormat }}"

  timeoutMs: 120000
  transport: binary
files.config.yaml:
# `characterId` and `characterGender` are GONE. They fed the retired multi-speaker compat path — see
# package.yaml — and nothing in apps/ sets them.

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [text]
  properties:
    text:
      type: string
      title: Text
      description: The words to speak.
      default: "{{{input}}}"
      "ui:field": template
    voiceId:
      type: string
      title: Voice ID
      description: >-
        Any voice id from your ElevenLabs library. Leave blank for a default narrator voice — the same
        premade voice the code version fell back to, so an unset field keeps working.
      default: ""
    modelId:
      type: string
      title: Model
      description: Override the TTS model. Leave blank for the package default.
      default: ""
    stability:
      type: number
      title: Stability
      description: >-
        0 is most expressive, 0.5 natural, 1 most consistent. ElevenLabs accepts ONLY these three values
        on this model, so anything else falls back to 0.5.
      enum: [0.0, 0.5, 1.0]
      enumNames: ["0 — expressive", "0.5 — natural", "1 — consistent"]
      default: 0.5
    outputFormat:
      type: string
      title: Output Format
      description: Audio encoding, e.g. mp3_44100_128. Leave blank for the account default.
      default: ""
"ui:order": [text, voiceId, stability, modelId, outputFormat]
files.interface.yaml:
inputs:
  - name: input
    type: string
    required: true
    description: The text to speak

outputs:
  - name: audio
    type: object
    description: "Generated audio: { data (base64), mimeType, fileName }"
  - name: metadata
    type: object
    description: format, voiceId, characters

credentials:
  - name: elevenlabsCredential
    required: true
files.node.yaml:
type: ElevenLabs
kind: PromiseNode

name: ElevenLabs TTS
category: Media & Design
color: "#FF69B4"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1768540562/gravity/icons/elevanlabs.jpg

description: Speak text aloud in a chosen voice. Outputs base64 MP3.

whenToUse: >-
  Read TEXT ALOUD in one voice: a narration, an announcement, a spoken reply. It performs words that are
  already written, so use it when the words exist and only the voice is needed. For several speakers in
  one clip use ElevenLabs Dialogue; for the sound of a thing rather than speech use Sound Effects.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
# Needs ELEVENLABS_API_KEY. Short text, because this bills per character.

testData:
  config:
    text: The glass box hums, and the city wakes.
    stability: 0.5
  inputs:
    input: The glass box hums, and the city wakes.
  expect:
    audio: >-
      return typeof output.audio.data === 'string'
        && output.audio.data.length > 1000
        && output.audio.mimeType.startsWith('audio/')
    # The DEFAULT voice must be reported, not an empty string: that fallback lives in two expressions and
    # this is what catches them disagreeing.
    metadata: "return output.metadata.voiceId.length > 0 && output.metadata.characters === 39"
